options: adsorption of ions from the solution
questions.solution: The colloidal particles have a tendency to preferentially adsorb a particular type of ions form the solution. This preferential adsorption of a particular type of ions imparts a particular type of charge to colloidal narticles.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Adsorption of a gas follows Freundlich adsorption isotherm. $x$ is the mass of the gas adsorbed on mass $m$ of the adsorbent. The plot of $\frac{x}{m}$ versus $\log p$ is shown in the given graph.
$\frac{x}{m}$ is proportional to :
questions.solution: According to Freundlich adsorption isotherm $\frac{x}{m} \propto p^{\frac{1}{n}}, \frac{x}{m}=k p^{\frac{1}{n}}$ Slope $=\frac{2}{3}\log \frac{x}{m}=\log k+\frac{1}{n} \log p$ Slope $=\frac{1}{n}=\frac{2}{3}\frac{x}{m} \propto p^{\frac{2}{3}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In Freundlich adsorption isotherm, the value of $1 / n$& is
options: always $1$ in case of physical adsorption
always $1$ in use of chemical adsorption
questions.solution:
Freundlich isotherm is related with the pressure of gas adsorbed, as follows $\dfrac{x}{m} = k \cdot p^{1 / n}$

where, $\dfrac{x}{m} =$ amount of gas~$\left(x\right)$ adsorbed over the surface of mass $\left(m\right)$.

$p =$ pressure of gas

$k =$ freundlich constant

Thus, value of $' n '$ is always greater than 1 and therefore value of $1 / n$ lies between $0 and 1$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following graph is correctly represented according to Freundlich isotherm.
questions.solution:
According to Freundlich adsorption isotherm,
$x / m = k \times P\dfrac{1}{n}$
where, $x =$ mass of gas adsorbed on mass '$m$' of the absorbent at pressure $p$.

$k$ and $n =$ constants.

Taking logarithm on both sides, we get
$logx / m = logk + \dfrac{1}{n}logp$

This is equation of a straight line with slope of $\dfrac{1}{n}$ and intercept of $logk$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following will be the most effective in the coagulation of $\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{OH})_{3}$ soil?
questions.solution: According to Hardy-Schulze rule, coagulation power of ions is directly proportional to charge on ion. $\because \mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{OH})_{3}$ is positively charged colloid. $\therefore$ It will be coagulated by anion. (a) $\mathrm{Mg}_{3}\left(\mathrm{PO}_{4}\right)_{2} \rightleftharpoons 3 \mathrm{Mg}^{2+}+2 \mathrm{PO}_{4}^{3-}$ (b) $\mathrm{BaCl}_{2} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Ba}^{2+}+2 \mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ (c) $\mathrm{NaCl} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Na}^{+}+\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ (d) $\mathrm{KCN} \rightleftharpoons \mathrmK^{+}+\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ Because $\mathrm{PO}_{4}^{3-}$ has highest charge among the given anions, therefore, $\mathrm{Mg}_{3}\left(\mathrm{PO}_{4}\right)_{2}$ is the most effective in the coagulation of $\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{OH})_{3}$ solution.
